0003 decision 5 (heavy): a first start is told from a lost journal by an explicit bootstrap command plus the authority ID repeated in the configuration as a witness; runner up: the explicit command alone
nodes.rationale: A daemon that finds an empty directory cannot know whether a journal ever existed; the configuration is the only other durable thing an operator controls, and the same value binds a configuration to its journal in both directions.

nodes.label: Cross check finding 14 of spec 0003: the reason given for the duplicate endpoint check was overstated; reworded: an alias that slips through closes writes, it never opens them
0003 decision 11 (heavy): the credential reference is the key credential_file in the identity entry, added now and read in 004; runner up: a separate [[credential]] table
0003 decision 13 (not heavy): the identity map is an exact pair, byte for byte, with no wildcard and no default; runner up: a wildcard for the database
0003 decision 14 (not heavy): routing_profile accepts 'primary' as default and refuses 'replica' with its own code; runner up: leave the key out until 007
0003 decision 9 (heavy): a finding inside a repeated table carries key and position, a fourth location; runner up: position only

Cross check major 1 of spec 0003: a conflict did not stay closed once the second primary was out of sight, against PRD-006 AC-2; fixed by decision 18 (the durable conflict latch, authority.conflict_latched, walk 3 row o)

Cross check finding 7 of spec 0003: two criteria promised things no test showed and the documentation comments had no check; compile_fail tests are named for AC-6 and AC-12, and AC-14 says its comment half is checked by reading

0003 decision 18 (heavy): a conflict stays closed when its evidence disappears, through a durable conflict latch per cluster set by the daemon and cleared only by an operation; runner up: a latch in memory only, or none
nodes.rationale: Added after the cross check: evidence that can disappear. The latch is the one case where an observation writes to the journal, acceptable because it can only restrict.

nodes.label: Cross check finding 10 of spec 0003: the pool key named a pool-control type that pool-core cannot see; the source is now the route view of pool-core, filled by the daemon

Spec 0003 rationale: Control and session data model rationale (context, four options, 27 decisions taken, evidence gathered, cross check findings, cross check of the update of 2026-11-15 and of the AC-16 addition, review of 2026-11-15)

Context of spec 0003: POOL is about to gain shared state; the login must come from an operator's map, the write target must be operator approved and confirmed by a probe right now, and a restart must not quietly change either; forces: no listener or PostgreSQL connection yet, tracer bullet, sixteen packages and no native code, every later slice reads these records
Spec 0003 option 3 (rejected): a spec only, with no build; the walks stay sentences, scope 004 grows and the scope's own Done when is left without evidence

Spec 0003 option 2 (rejected): also build the SQLite journal now with offline commands to create and inspect it; bootstrap would lack evidence from PostgreSQL, SQLite is native code needing a license decision by a person, and a dedicated writer needs a thread that rule W3 forbids

Cross check finding 6 of spec 0003: the new W4 check would fail the existing test tree and the evidence of step 1 could not run before its commit; the test helper gets a source line and the proving script runs after the commit

Decisions taken for spec 0003: 27 choices made in the auto decision mode, each the recommended option with its runner up and the way back; heavy marks a public contract, a format on disk or a part of the security model (18 heavy); decisions 20 to 27 were added by the updates of 2026-11-15
0003 decision 10 (not heavy): the valid report does not show the new tables and stays as spec 0001 defines it; runner up: counts of clusters, nodes and identities
0003 decision 12 (heavy): default telemetry may name identifiers, generations and reason names, never principal, logins, database names, hosts or paths; runner up: allow principal and login names
0003 decision 15 (heavy): missing evidence about a replica does not close writes, only a positive conflict does, and bootstrap needs every node once; runner up: every node must be fresh for a write
nodes.rationale: Applying fail closed to every node would let the least reliable replica decide the availability of the primary.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 16 (not heavy): W4 and W5 learn the packages from the manifests as today, plus a check of path packages in the lockfile; runner up: read the dependency edges from the lockfile
0003 decision 17 (heavy): a quarantined node that says it is a primary does not close writes; runner up: it does
nodes.rationale: A fenced former primary is exactly the node most likely to misbehave; it must not hold the cluster after an operation that was done right.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 1 (heavy): scope 003 builds configuration keys and a plain authority model, the journal file in 004; runner up: build the SQLite journal now
0003 decision 2 (heavy): the authority model lives in a third crate, crates/pool-control; runner up: wait for 004 or a module in pool-config

0003 decision 6 (heavy): a supported backup carries the hold, reconcile gives the journal a new authority ID, and the timeline rule catches part of a raw copy; runner up: a witness file outside the journal or comparing the inode
nodes.rationale: A restored journal is correct about the past and silent about everything since; it may not speak until an operator has compared it with the present. Unsolved: a raw copy or a VM snapshot rollback with the old writer up.

nodes.label: Spec 0003 option 1 (chosen): configuration keys and a plain, tested authority model now; the journal file in 004
nodes.rationale: What this scope can prove without input or output is exactly the part that carries the safety argument; functions over values make three way agreement checkable over 8192 cases and make closed the only accidental result. The price is an interface built ahead of its caller.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 4 (heavy): the configuration names the writer with one key per cluster, expected_writer, that must keep agreeing with the journal; runner up: a role key on every node or a bootstrap only key
nodes.rationale: Safety contract 8 says configuration conflicts fail closed; a key read once and then ignored cannot contradict anything. The price: after a promotion the file must be updated before writes open.

nodes.label: Cross check finding 11 of spec 0003: scope 004 needs a lock on the state directory, a way to read the authority ID again and a current timeline source; added to Follow-up 4
Cross check finding 13 of spec 0003: the glossary rows Observation and Approved writer still say backend for a server; it became document correction 4

Cross check major 2 of spec 0003: the journal did not record the nodes, so editing the file could hide evidence; fixed by decision 19 (the member table, the wider authority.config_conflict, walk 3 row p)

Cross check major 3 of spec 0003: the start wrote to the journal before classifying it and could change the journal of another daemon; the start now reads and classifies first and writes only in Ready
Cross check finding 4 of spec 0003: the lookup index of the identity map could print names through a derived Debug; the index is now its own private type with a hand written Debug
Cross check finding 8 of spec 0003: derives and Display of the new types were not given; they are now stated for both crates
Cross check finding 9 of spec 0003: one fixture description could be read two ways; reworded

Cross check of spec 0003: an independent read by another model (Claude Opus, read only) on 2026-11-15 of the first draft raised 14 gaps and 7 soundness findings; all were taken under the auto decision mode and none is left open

Evidence gathered for spec 0003 (not product evidence): finding positions read with toml 1.2.1 and serde 1.0.229 through toml::Spanned on 2026-11-15; the four CREATE TABLE statements and pragmas run with sqlite3 3.54.0; the validation time of the AC-15 made inputs measured on an Apple M1 Max; prove-checks case 9 uses crates/pool-core and case 17 depends on the word planned
0003 decision 19 (heavy): the journal records the nodes of a cluster as members, and a member missing from the configuration is a conflict; runner up: record the writer only
nodes.rationale: Added after the cross check: a node deleted from the file would have stopped being asked.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 7 (heavy): the journal is one SQLite file with application_id and user_version, strict tables and forward migrations applied at start; runner up: an explicit migration command
0003 decision 3 (heavy): a configured server is called a node, table [[node]]; runner up: backend, table [[backend]]
nodes.rationale: The glossary gives backend one meaning, a connection POOL opens; calling the server a backend too would give one word two meanings in the pool key.

nodes.label: Spec 0003 option 4 (rejected): put the authority model into pool-config; it saves three baseline lines but breaks the boundary the repository structure sets, and it would have to move in 004

0003 decision 8 (heavy): topology epoch, authority revision and start sequence survive a restart in the journal; all other generations live in memory, scoped by the start sequence; runner up: a durable configuration generation
nodes.rationale: Without the start sequence a configuration generation of 2 before a restart and one after it are indistinguishable; one durable counter that scopes every memory generation is smaller than making each durable.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 20 (not heavy): the time of validation is a criterion, a new AC-15 with Build plan step 8; runner up: widen the rule under Keys and add no criterion, or make it a part of AC-3
nodes.rationale: Without a criterion nothing fails when the counting goes back to once per entry: the old rule named only the uniqueness and reference checks, so its letter was met while validate took 12 s (release) and 241 s (debug) for a valid file of 16000 nodes. A new ID is used because AC-1 to AC-6 already have recorded evidence; inside AC-3 the milestone 2 evidence would have to be taken again.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 21 (not heavy): the validation time bound covers an invalid file and a file with every entry on one line; runner up: valid files only
nodes.rationale: The daemon of scope 004 runs the same function at start, and a start that hangs for minutes on a generated file with a repeated mistake defeats the 1 MiB limit. The one line shape was measured (12000 inline tables, 16 s in a release build) and is the shape where the obvious repair, a table of line starts, is still quadratic. With the runner up made input 3 goes away.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 22 (not heavy): validation time is checked by an upper limit of 10 seconds on one call, in the debug build of cargo test, on three inputs at the file limit, plus one small input whose findings come against file order; runner up: a ratio between a half size and a full size input, or a release build timed by hand in the verification record
nodes.rationale: A ratio divides two timings of a fraction of a second, and one pause of the machine moves it past any threshold; a run by hand is not repeated by CI. The absolute limit sits about 25 times above the correct code and about 16 times below the broken code. A test cannot interrupt the call (rule W3 allows no thread), so a regression runs for minutes and then fails; slow, and still red.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 23 (not heavy): a cluster with a failed id does not stop cross check 3 for all clusters; that cluster alone is passed over, as the opening sentence of step 6 already said; runner up: skip the whole check
nodes.rationale: Skipping the whole check would let a bad cluster id hide a wrong expected_writer in another cluster until the next run.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 24 (heavy): the system identifier, the authority ID and the timeline ID may appear in log fields and default diagnostics, never as metric labels, and the observed role may also be a label; runner up: never by default for the system identifier, [REDACTED] in Debug
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL does not treat the system identifier as a secret (pg_control_system() returns it, IDENTIFY_SYSTEM answers with it), it is no credential, and it is the one value that explains an identity mismatch. Against: it names a cluster for its whole life and its upper bits hold the initialization time; neither opens a door. Redaction would cost a hand written Debug on every type that carries the number. Metric labels are held back because a label is copied onto every sample and often leaves the host.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 25 (heavy): a generation may not be a metric label, only a log field or the value of a metric, which narrows what decision 12 allowed; runner up: leave generations in the label column
nodes.rationale: Generations only grow, so as labels they are values without a bound, against T-12. No code changes either way, because nothing writes a metric yet.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 26 (heavy): a Ready state is tied to the configuration that confirmed it, in code now: writer_admission compares the witness again, with a new AC-16 and Build plan step 9; runner up: text only, one sentence under writer admission and a rule for the reload of 009
nodes.rationale: The checker of milestone 3 passed a state classified Ready under witness X with a configuration with no witness, and with one with witness Y, and got Open both times. The case arrives with the reload of scope 009, and the spec nowhere else relies on a later slice reading a rule. The identity of the journal was the one agreement checked only once; comparing it again costs one comparison of 16 bytes and changes no signature and no reason name. The price is a second small build step after the feature was verified and one more criterion.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 27 (not heavy): TimelineId and MonotonicTime may derive Hash and the spec now lists it; runner up: remove the derive from the code
nodes.rationale: Removing the derive would be a Build plan step that deletes two words and buys nothing.

Review of 2026-11-15 section of the spec 0003 rationale: the independent review of the range ca9a897..be06393 ended with approve with nits (no blocker, no major finding, 15 minor findings, 18 nits); scope 003 closes on the verified tree; the update adds no criterion, Build plan step or decision, changes no code, and had no cross check because nothing was decided in it

Why nothing changes now (0003 review of 2026-11-15): m1, m2 and m3 are limits of what the caller of writer_admission passes in and no caller exists yet; closing them in code now would mean guessing the shape of the journal reader and of the probe list before scope 004 designs either; so each is named where the rule lives and again in Follow-up 4

0003 review of 2026-11-15, m1 sorted (a Ready state cannot learn of a later latch): a duty of scope 004 with a recommended shape and a test it owes; recorded in Follow-up 4 and in notes under writer admission, after walk 3 and in the first consequence about open admission
nodes.rationale: A function in pool-control is the recommended shape: reading the journal again after every write also works but leaves the failed write to the memory of the daemon. A function that turns a Ready state and a closed answer into a Ready state with the latch set needs no journal, covers that case too, and the latch cannot be forgotten by a caller (the argument of decision 26). It stays a recommendation: the architect of scope 004 decides.

nodes.label: 0003 review of 2026-11-15, m2 sorted (any crate can build a journal value): a duty of scope 004 when the journal reader is built; recorded in Follow-up 4 and in the same consequence as m1

0003 review of 2026-11-15, m3 sorted (a sample after now or a repeated sample hides a second primary): two duties of the caller and one question for scope 004; recorded in Follow-up 4 and the note under the rule Fresh

0003 review of 2026-11-15, m4 sorted (the lockfile check of W4 has one way around it): work for the next slice that touches tools/repo-check; recorded in Follow-up 10, the note under Workspace and guards and one sentence in Follow-up 10 of spec 0002
0003 review of 2026-11-15, m5 sorted (two million findings from one file): a decision for the user, with three options and a recommendation; recorded in Follow-up 11
nodes.rationale: The recommendation is both, in two steps. The buffer removes one system call per finding and changes nothing a user can see, so it needs no decision; it bounds neither memory nor output size. A limit does, and it changes a public contract: AC-3 says the whole configuration is reported in one run, and a last line saying findings were left out is new output under spec 0001. So the user decides it, before the first start of the daemon in scope 004.

nodes.label: 0003 review of 2026-11-15, m6 sorted (the cost of one admission): a question for scope 004, or scope 008; recorded in Follow-up 4

0003 review of 2026-11-15, m8 sorted (control characters above U+007F): a gap, not a choice; closing it changes which files are valid; recorded in Follow-up 12 and the note at the name syntax
nodes.rationale: No decision in the list covers the control character list; it was written as the ASCII set and never weighed against the rest of Unicode. Decision 12 keeps names out of default telemetry, which is why nothing is exposed today. Refusing more characters makes files invalid that are valid now, so it is a change of behavior and not part of this update.

nodes.label: 0003 review of 2026-11-15, d1 sorted (row k against the letter of PRD-006 AC-2): the exception is now stated where the PRD is cited and the note in the PRD is for the user; recorded in Follow-up 13 and Follow-up 7 and in notes under the criteria, under writer admission and after walk 3
